patients.summary: Thin never-smoking man who joins in 2018 with lifelong seasonal allergic rhinitis and exercise intolerance; allergen immunotherapy from 2020, mitochondrial myopathy diagnosed by neurology in 2021, PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with lower-lobe emphysema and mildly raised transaminases diagnosed by pulmonology in 2023. Schizophrenia diagnosed at a June 2026 psychiatric admission, followed a week after discharge by an ED observation stay for benztropine anticholinergic toxicity; benztropine stopped, risperidone continues.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

27M here to establish care. No PCP for a few years since aging out of his childhood practice. Main thing he wants is to keep his allergy meds going.

Allergies (nose/eyes): every spring and again in early fall since he was a kid. Sneezing fits, stuffy nose, itchy watery eyes, drip down the back of the throat. Uses cetirizine 10 mg on bad days and fluticasone 2 sprays each side daily through the season. Says these take the edge off but don't fully control it. Never seen an allergist, never skin tested.

Stamina: says he has always run out of gas before other people. Played sports as a kid and kept up for the most part, but was the first one winded and done. Works construction and gets through the day. Not something he came in about, mentions it when asked about exercise. No chest pain, no palpitations, no fainting.

PMH: seasonal allergic rhinitis. Otherwise none.
PSH: tonsillectomy at age 12.
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PO once daily PRN; fluticasone nasal 2 sprays/nostril daily.
Allergies: tree pollen, grass pollen. NKDA.

Family hx:
- Mother: mitochondrial myopathy; her symptoms started in her 30s.
- Father: died in his mid-40s of cirrhosis, which the family put down to drinking. Pt recalls he had breathing problems for years.
- Paternal grandmother: cirrhosis, cause never known.
- Maternal uncle: schizophrenia.
- Maternal side: several relatives with hearing loss starting young.
- Identical twin brother, healthy.

Social: construction laborer. Never smoked, no vaping. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a week, social. No drugs. No pets.

ROS: negative except as above. No weight change, no fevers, no cough, no GI or urinary complaints.

Exam:
BP 116/75, HR 68, RR 15, T 36.8, SpO2 98% RA. Wt 65.2 kg, Ht 179.2 cm, BMI 20.3.
Gen: thin, well appearing, NAD.
HEENT: nasal mucosa pale and mildly boggy, no polyps. TMs clear. Oropharynx clear, tonsils surgically absent. Conjunctivae mildly injected.
Neck: supple, no LAD, thyroid not enlarged.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: clear bilaterally, good air movement.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema.
Skin: no rashes.
Neuro: alert, CN grossly intact, strength and gait normal.

A/P:
1. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, pollen. Partial control on current regimen. Continue cetirizine PRN and daily fluticasone during the season. Can send Rx to pharmacy so Medicaid covers them. Discussed technique with the spray (aim away from septum).
2. Exercise intolerance, lifelong by his description. Exam unremarkable today. Will keep an eye on it.
3. Health maintenance: Tdap given today (last tetanus >10 yr by his report). One-time HIV and hep C screening offered and accepted, drawn with CBC and BMP. Flu shot when supply arrives next month. Never smoker.

RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn. He has the practice cell for texts.

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Thanks for coming in today, Tyler.

What we did: tetanus/whooping cough booster (Tdap). Blood work: blood count, chemistry panel, HIV and hepatitis C screening. Results will come through the portal in a few days.

Your medicines: keep using cetirizine 10 mg once a day when your allergies act up, and fluticasone nasal spray 2 sprays each side once a day during allergy season. Point the spray toward the outside of each nostril.

Next steps: flu shot in October (nurse visit is fine). Yearly physical next September.

You can call or text the practice line any time.

documents.title: Lab Results Released
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tyler, your labs from Tuesday are all normal: blood counts normal (hemoglobin 14.8), kidney function and electrolytes normal (creatinine 0.97, sodium 141, potassium 4.1), glucose 89. HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to do here. Watch for a message from us about flu shots in October.

documents.title: Records From Prior Practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from patient's former pediatric/family practice, 38 pages, scanned to media.

Abstracted by front desk for PCP review:
- Routine well-child and adolescent visits through age 18. Growth along the lower percentiles for weight, normal development documented.
- Childhood immunization series recorded complete. Td at age 16 (2007).
- Tonsillectomy at age 12 (2004), no complications.
- Seasonal allergy complaints noted at several spring visits, treated with OTC antihistamine and later a nasal steroid spray.
- Sports physicals cleared every year.
- No hospitalizations. No labs of note.

PCP reviewed 9/19: nothing new. Tdap given 9/11 appropriately.

documents.title: Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after work for flu vaccine. Screening questions negative: no fever today, no egg allergy, no prior vaccine reactions. Quadrivalent inactivated influenza 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated well, left ambulatory after 15 min.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

Tyler is 28, here for his yearly. Feels fine. Spring was a rough allergy season, used the spray every day and the cetirizine most days April through June, and the fall stretch is starting now. Still working construction. Same as last year with stamina, no change he can point to.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN, fluticasone nasal daily in season.
Allergies: tree/grass pollen. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk, no drugs.
PHQ-2: 0.

Vitals: BP 114/69, HR 78, RR 16, T 36.8, SpO2 97% RA, Wt 66.1 kg, BMI 20.6.

Exam:
Gen: thin, NAD.
HEENT: turbinates pale and swollen, clear rhinorrhea. Oropharynx clear.
Neck: no LAD.
CV: regular, no murmur.
Resp: clear, no wheeze.
Abd: soft, NT, no HSM.
Skin: no lesions of concern.
Neuro: nonfocal.

Assessment/plan:
- Well adult exam. Fasting lipids (first one), CBC, BMP drawn.
- Allergic rhinitis, seasonal: same regimen, refills on file.
- Exercise intolerance: stable by history.
- Flu vaccine today.
- Tdap done 2018.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Physical Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tyler, everything from your physical looks good. Cholesterol panel: total 158, LDL 84, HDL 58, triglycerides 78, all in a healthy range, no need to repeat for several years. Blood count, kidney numbers and sugar are normal too.
